glosses: to eat up (usually avariciously)
geheel opeten

examples.text: Hij had in een mum van tijd twee stukken pizza verorberd en stortte zich op een derde.
Tot nu toe werd de invloed van zwarte gaten alleen indirect gezien: door de straling die ze uitstoten wanneer ze te rommelig het materiaal in hun omgeving verorberen.

glosses: To use up.

examples.text: The power plant consumes 30 tons of coal per hour.

glosses: To eat.

examples.text: Baby birds consume their own weight in food each day.

Concerns were raised around the ability of Milky Way species to consume proteins from Andromeda, so seed banks formed a significant part of the arks' cargo. We now know it is safe to consume food grown or hunted here, though enzyme supplements are recommended and have become a social norm at mealtimes.

glosses: To completely occupy the thoughts or attention of.

examples.text: Desire consumed him.

glosses: To destroy completely.

examples.text: The building was consumed by fire.
If he were putting to my house the brand / That shall consume it.

Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon the earth, where moth and rust consume, and where thieves break through and steal: but lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth consume, and where thieves do not break through to steal: […]

glosses: To waste away slowly.

examples.text: Therefore, let Benedick, like cover'd fire, / Consume away in sighs.
But, sir, you see how weak I am. You must see that I have been consuming from day to day […].
He assured her the child was consuming at that moment in the next room.

glosses: To trade money for good or services as an individual.

examples.text: In a materialistic society, individuals are taught to consume, consume, consume.
If you consume this product while in Japan, you may be subject to consumption tax.

glosses: To absorb information, especially through the mass media.

examples.text: The Internet has changed the way we consume news.

glosses: To consume completely.

examples.text: He was so hungry that he ate up everything on his plate.
Dinner is served. Eat up!

glosses: To cause (someone) to obsess; to figuratively consume (someone).

examples.text: His anger has been eating him up.

glosses: To subtract, use up.

examples.text: His behavior has eaten up all the goodwill we felt towards him.
The powerful car ate up the miles.

glosses: To accept or believe entirely, immediately, and without questioning.

examples.text: She ate up everything that her image consultant said.

glosses: To acclaim or praise (someone or something).

examples.text: They eat up every book he puts out.
Onstage at the fund-raiser beside Mr. Obama and Jimmy Kimmel, Mr. Biden laughed along, cracked a joke or two, and slammed the Supreme Court. The audience ate it up.

glosses: To find something to be very cute.

examples.text: You're so cute, I could just eat you up!

glosses: To go quickly on a route.

examples.text: We ate up the road to Pennsylvania.
You're gonna have to eat up the whole way there.

glosses: To be very good at; to succeed at; to smash. (Compare eat and leave no crumbs.)

examples.text: One fan shared a snippet from the music video wherein Jungkook and Han So-hee are drowning in water. Despite the catastrophic situation, the lovers are squabbling with each other. The fan commented: “The laundromat cause they ate that up”.

glosses: To completely dominate someone else, especially with a comeback or clapback.

examples.text: Girl, you ate him up!

glosses: To consume, deplete, expend, or exhaust.

examples.text: "My third command to the Winged Monkeys," said Glinda, "shall be to carry you to your forest. Then, having used up the powers of the Golden Cap, I shall give it to the King of the Monkeys, that he and his band may thereafter be free for evermore."
The All Blacks drove upfield, using up the remaining moments, and when Joubert blew for another French infringement, the biggest party in New Zealand's history was under way.

glosses: To take or occupy.
Hacer uso, disfrutar de un bien o de un servicio.
Utilizar bienes materiales como alimentos, combustibles y otros, que son destruidos o agotados con su uso.
Usar algo, explotarlo, hasta su término o agotamiento.
Deteriorar a una persona una preocupación, enfermedad u otro mal.
Savourer, déguster.
Engloutir, avaler, dévorer.

examples.text: Hij verorberde een hele kip.
examples.translation: Il s’est farci un poulet entier.
